transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Honestly, I'm only here because people keep saying I'm way too thin and need help. An urgent care doctor and my friends are making a huge deal out of it, but I don't really see what the big problem is with my weight being this low.
How do you see your body when you look in the mirror, especially compared to how others might see you?

When I look in the mirror, I don't see the "dangerously thin" person everyone else claims to see, and I honestly think they're all overreacting. Instead, I just zero in on areas like my stomach or thighs if they don't look completely razor-thin, which makes me feel like I've failed and haven't been disciplined enough.
Can you describe your eating habits over the past few months? Specifically, have you been avoiding certain foods or restricting your intake because of concerns about gaining weight?

Most days I just power through on black coffee and maybe a granola bar at night to save money and stay focused on my painting. If I even think about eating heavier things like burgers or pizza, I get this intense panic that I'll wake up looking softer or heavier overnight. To avoid that, I usually just skip eating with others and say I already ate.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently, and do you have a fear of gaining weight even if you're underweight?

I've definitely lost weight—my clothes are hanging off me and my belt is on its last hole—but I see it as a sign of discipline rather than a problem. I do have an intense panic about gaining weight, and even thinking about eating heavier foods makes me worry I'll wake up 'softer' or heavier overnight, which is why I avoid eating with others.
